5post_crm.name: 5post_crm
5post_crm.title: 5 Post – Parcel Locker Control System
text:
Implementation details

Within the scope of the UMS (Post Office Management System) Administrator Module, a comprehensive UI/UX design process was carried out to deliver the MVP and subsequent enhancements. The team conducted business analysis, stakeholder interviews, user flow mapping, and built a foundational UI kit. Close collaboration with developers and potential end-users helped clarify requirements and tackle interface challenges not covered by standard Material Design components. Work was organized in multiple phases, addressing identified risks (e.g., discrepancies between Miro and wiki documentation, limited research data, insufficient test users) and optimizing time usage.

Application functionality

  • Devices Control;
  • Parcel Control;
  • Database management;
  • Transactions and expenses control;
  • Invoice generating and tracking;

Development Plan

Adopting an agile mindset, the team progressed in short, iterative sprints, each focused on refining a specific set of features. Frequent check-ins ensured close collaboration between designers, developers, and stakeholders. This approach allowed for rapid adaptation to evolving requirements, early identification of risks, and efficient integration of user feedback. Each sprint concluded with a thorough review, maintaining a clear handoff between design and development efforts while preserving quality and consistency across the entire solution.

Project results

Over the course of the project (43 days in total for UI/UX tasks), key modules such as Orders, Parcel Control, Postamats, Users, Software Update, Inventory, Organizations, and Incidents were implemented. Each module included multiple pages, from basic information to logbooks, notifications, security logs, and advanced editing features. This phased approach enabled efficient iterative design, minimized risks, and ensured alignment with both business objectives and user expectations. Ultimately, the resulting admin panel successfully consolidated all required functionality—monitoring devices, managing parcel lockers and orders, maintaining databases, and generating invoices—delivering an end-to-end solution that met the client's needs and timelines.

busuu.name: busuu
busuu.title: Busuu.com – Language Learning Platform
text:
About

Busuu is a leading EdTech platform that combines AI-powered language learning with social interaction. With over 15M active learners worldwide, the product continuously evolves to improve user engagement, retention, and learning experience.

My Role

As a Product Designer at Busuu, I worked across two cross-functional squads — Logos and Phoenix. My responsibilities included UX research, interaction and visual design, prototyping, and design handoff to engineering teams. I collaborated closely with Product Managers, Learning Designers, and Developers to deliver data-informed, scalable design solutions.

Logos Squad — Internal CMS for Course Creation

The Logos Squad focused on building an internal tool (CMS) that empowered Busuu’s Learning Designers to efficiently create, translate, and publish new courses. My goal was to simplify complex workflows inherited from the legacy Slate system, improve usability, and introduce automation for content translation using AI.

Key features I designed and delivered:

  • Content Generation Flow: Redesigned from scratch the process for creating courses, lessons, and activities with a cleaner UI and faster onboarding experience.
  • Preview Mode: Enabled real-time visualization of content across Web, Mobile, and Tablet layouts — allowing designers to detect layout or copy issues early.
  • AI-assisted Translation Workflow: Introduced download/upload translation features integrated with automated word count, translator context fields, and AI-assisted content preparation — reducing manual CSV editing time by 70%.
  • String Reuse System: Designed the search & reuse interface to prevent content duplication and improve consistency across courses.

Through iterative design reviews and Miro workshops, we significantly improved tool usability and reduced the learning curve for new designers. The redesign led to faster content production and better visibility over the course lifecycle.

Phoenix Squad — Renewal & Retention Flows

The Phoenix Squad worked on user monetization and retention across iOS, Android, and Web. Our mission: reduce churn, increase renewal rates, and re-engage lapsed users through personalization and behavioral insights.

Core initiatives I led:

  • Cancellation Flow (Dynamic Exit Survey): Designed a personalized flow that adapts to users’ cancellation reasons. For cost-related cancellations, users received a 20% retention offer. This reduced churn and improved renewal intent.
  • Countdown Clock: Introduced a visual countdown to premium expiry, increasing urgency to renew and reducing involuntary churn caused by failed payments.
  • Progress & Achievements in Cancel Flow: Added progress visualization (lessons completed, streaks, XP) at the cancellation point — reframing value and preventing impulsive cancellations.
  • Tailored Paywalls for Lapsed Users: Designed personalized paywalls referencing user history and learning progress, improving win-back conversions compared to generic variants.
  • One-tap Cancellation Reversal: Created contextual prompts allowing users to instantly reverse a cancellation after using a premium feature — integrated across all platforms.

Each initiative went through hypothesis framing, UX exploration, visual design, and A/B testing readiness. I collaborated with analytics and marketing teams to ensure measurable impact and consistency across touchpoints.

Impact

  • Reduced cancellation completion rate in tested cohorts by up to 12%.
  • Improved content creation efficiency for Learning Designers by 2x after Logos rollout.
  • Delivered unified design patterns across internal tools and customer-facing products using Busuu’s Design System.

Project results

This project taught me the value of designing for both end users and internal stakeholders — aligning UX consistency, operational efficiency, and business outcomes. Working across multiple squads at Busuu helped me strengthen collaboration, rapid prototyping, and data-driven design iteration skills.

cognni.name: cognni
cognni.title: Cognni.ai
about: Cognni.ai is a cutting-edge Cloud Information Security Assistant that empowers organizations to map and visualize their critical data assets with clarity and actionable insights. By translating complex security events into clear visual narratives, Cognni.ai bridges communication gaps between CISOs, CEOs, and department heads, driving strategic decision-making.
text:
Project Overview

Cognni.ai is designed to simplify the complex world of information security by offering a user-friendly interface that emphasizes clear descriptions and intents. The focus is on mapping the relationships between data, people, and events, ensuring that even non-technical stakeholders can understand the current information state and necessary actions.

Goals and Objectives

  • Reduce incident response time to the defined MTTR threshold.
  • Simplify data comprehension — visualize “people ↔ data ↔ events” relationships in 1–2 clicks.
  • Adapt the interface to specific roles (CISO, CEO, department heads) via personalized dashboards.
  • Embed collaboration and delegation so remediation tasks are closed without repeated escalations.

User Research & Journey Mapping

In-depth research, including user journey mapping, revealed that clients greatly value our ability to visually map data relationships. They need to see how employees, departments, and files interconnect to understand security risks and responsibilities. This insight drove our design strategy.

Design and UX Solutions

The design approach centered on clarity and usability. Key solutions included:

  • Interactive visualizations and iconography that clearly illustrate data relationships and security events.
  • Explicit delegation sections in the UI that allow CISOs to assign responsibility to department heads.
  • A simplified, jargon-free language that makes the interface accessible to all stakeholders.

These design choices ensure that users can quickly identify anomalies, understand data domains (such as HR or Finance), and act on security insights.

Challenges and Iterations

Throughout the project, several challenges emerged, including:

  • Ambiguous labels and internal terminology (e.g., 'clusters', 'copies', 'versions') that confused users.
  • The need for a 'Cognni Dictionary' to clarify these terms and ensure consistency.
  • Balancing the technical details required for security analysis with a user-friendly presentation for non-technical audiences.

Iterative testing and feedback sessions allowed us to refine these elements for optimal clarity and usability.

Prototyping and Testing

Rapid prototyping and usability tests with target users (including CISOs and department heads) were crucial. These sessions helped validate our visualizations, delegation workflows, and overall navigation, ensuring that the final interface met the diverse needs of its users.

Results and Impact

The redesigned Cognni.ai interface now delivers a clear, actionable view of complex security data. By focusing on mapping over detection and streamlining communication between various organizational roles, the solution enables users to derive actionable insights, present clear strategic options to CEOs/Board, and drive meaningful change in their security practices.

verbling.name: verbling
verbling.title: Verbling – Online Language Tutoring Platform
text:
Goals and OKRs

The primary objective for the Verbling project was to create a seamless and engaging user journey that directly translates into measurable business growth. Our goals were centered on reducing friction in the registration and onboarding processes while enhancing the overall user experience. Specifically, we set clear OKRs to increase the conversion rate from free trial to first order by at least 15%, boost daily new registrations by 20%, and decrease the drop-off rate during the initial user interactions by 25%. Additionally, we aimed to refine the tutor discovery process—through improved search, filtering, and information presentation—to drive higher engagement and satisfaction. These targets were supported by a series of quantitative KPIs, including conversion metrics, customer satisfaction scores, and revenue impact estimates, ensuring that every UX improvement aligned with and contributed to the platform's strategic business outcomes.

Project details

In this project, I was responsible for conducting user research to understand the needs and pain points of both learners and teachers. I performed user testing using usertesting.com, conducted interviews with users via Intercom, and gathered quantitative data through user surveys. Based on these comprehensive insights, I created wireframes and prototypes to enhance the user experience. The final visual design not only made the platform more intuitive and engaging for users but also contributed to achieving key business OKRs by significantly boosting user engagement and conversion rates.

Onboarding

The onboarding initiative for Verbling is designed to provide new users with a clear, intuitive introduction to the platform before registration, enabling them to quickly understand its value proposition and efficiently connect with a suitable teacher, ultimately increasing user engagement and registration rates.

event_management_tool.name: event_management_tool
event_management_tool.title: Glenis Solutions – Event Management Tool
text:
Goals

The project aims to create a modern, user-friendly event management system for senior communities. By enhancing the interface and adding a robust validation process, the system will simplify event planning and approval while boosting resident engagement.

About tool

Event management software is one way to make senior living better. EMT is a system with ability to create and submit events for review, used to manage event calendars for guests. Residents stay involved and active in their communities. The challenge is to modernize the user interface and add a validation process. Another thing it's a mobile app to expand software capabilities.

Application functionality

  • Working with events;
  • Duplicate events;
  • Master Calendar feature;
  • Roll forward;
  • Existing features improvements;
Design process

Interviews

As a part of the qualitative research, I've conducted a number of interviews with users in various roles. Both users with administrative access rights and regular system users were interviewed.

Empathy map

To highlight a number of potentially important hypotheses, I created an average system user empathy map, which helps identify the most important hypotheses that I was going to confirm with a quantitative research in the next step.

Receiving data using google forms

As part of quantitative research to confirm previously derived hypotheses, I conducted a quantitative research and identified the most successful solutions, which were later implemented at the prototyping stage.

Current Calendar Process

One of the tasks was to change and improve the current process of updating events from the calendar, this process took a large amount of time and was not always convenient.

I have automated this process by removing unnecessary links in the chain and finalizing the remaining blocks using the new features of the application.

Wireframes

Once the list of MVP features has been approved by the stakeholders, I've started creating prototypes based on the data obtained from research.

Styled components library

Before starting the design phase, we created a shared design library.

Visual design

As a result of the visual design phase, a number of screens were built. This is important both for creating use cases and for developers use. In addition, some of the users who agreed to usability testing were invited to test the new application design.
Mocks

Mobile attendance

After research, I've decided to move some of the functionality from the main application to a mobile attendance mobile application.
  • An option to mark no attendance added;
  • An abillity to create a meal event and take an attendance;
  • Admins can track and consume statisticks.

Project results

The Customer was highly satisfied. He left positive feedback for Andersen. He recommended Andersen as a good contractor for software solutions for his colleagues from other financial organizations. The project was delivered quickly and on time, to the customer’s full satisfaction. The resulting solution encompasses all the required financial needs.

guy_carpenter.name: guy_carpenter
guy_carpenter.title: Guy Carpenter – Tax Calculator
text:
Goals

The team needed a web tool (internally referred to as the “Tax Calculator” or “Limits & Attachment Tool”) that would automate and streamline the process of combining reinsurance data, filtering policies, and calculating premiums and taxes across different regions, lines of business, and date ranges.

Design Challenge

  1. Complex Data Structures — The application must handle multiple file formats (CSV, Excel, UFC, Arium, etc.) and display comprehensive metadata (Treaty Name, Cedent, Line of Business, etc.).
  2. Multiple Filters & Profiles — Users require advanced filtering (by region, business unit, country) and the ability to segment by limit and attachment point.
  3. Tax & Premium Calculations — The interface needs to clearly present data on premium amounts, policy counts, and total sums, accommodating various regional tax rates.
  4. User Variability — Reinsurance analysts, underwriters, actuaries, and finance teams each need different views and outputs.

Key UX Objectives

  • Clarity and Efficiency: The interface should quickly guide users through data selection, filtering, and output generation without overwhelming them.
  • Flexible Customization: Filters, date ranges, and attachment buckets should be easy to configure for diverse reinsurance needs.
  • Seamless Data Visualization: A clean, organized layout helps users interpret large data sets at a glance.

UX Research & Discovery

Stakeholder interviews helped identify how analysts and underwriters search, filter, and merge data. User journey mapping revealed the core tasks: importing files, applying filters and profiles, reviewing limit and attachment breakdowns, setting date parameters, and exporting data. Competitive and internal tool analyses highlighted pain points in existing spreadsheets and analytics solutions.

Information Architecture

A two-panel layout was introduced: a left-side panel for file selection and filter options, and a main area for data visualization. Advanced features like date range pickers and multiple filter sets use progressive disclosure, ensuring a clear workflow. Responsive design ensures usability on various screen sizes.

User Flow Overview

  1. Select Files — Users pick relevant files from a list.
  2. Apply Filters — Filters are set for line of business, region, dates, etc.
  3. Review Data Table — The interface shows premiums, policy counts, and coverage layers by limit buckets.
  4. Adjust Dates — Users refine 'In Force' or 'Inception/Expiration' ranges if needed.
  5. Export & Download — Chosen data can be exported in multiple formats or consolidated in a single report.

Outcome & Learnings

The tool reduced manual spreadsheet work by an estimated 50%, significantly improving speed and accuracy in tax and premium calculations. The flexible, modular design allows quick adaptation for new lines of business or regulatory changes. Overall, the user-centric approach delivered a streamlined solution that better supports the reinsurance workflow.
